source: MazeMap building 1014912 polygons (map/source/mazemap/) and the route graph of the venue package

frame.venue: x = metres east, y = metres north of geo_origin (SW corner of the building outline's bounding box), z = metres up; floor 1 at z = 0. Same frame as map/research-techno-plaza.json
frame.gltf: right-handed Y-up: X = x (east), Y = z (up), Z = -y (south). Venue (x, y, z) -> glTF (x, z, -y); glTF (X, Y, Z) -> venue (X, -Z, Y)

unity.note: Unity is left-handed Y-up. Both common importers, UnityGLTF (SchemaExtensions CoordinateSpaceConversionScale = (-1, 1, 1)) and glTFast 4+, mirror X on import.
unity.as imported (X mirrored): Unity position = (-x, z, -y): Unity +x is west, +z is south. RouteCameraFollower.cs uses this with Flip X ticked (its default)
unity.after rotating the imported root 180 deg: Unity position = (x, z, y): x east, y up, z north (untick Flip X on the follower)

gltf_nodes: one node per level named L1..L9 (node extras carry floor and z); one mesh primitive per material

floor.used_for: floor slab (top at z): room floors

corridor.used_for: corridor / lobby floor plate (z..z+0.02), polished light-to-mid grey terrazzo with fine 2-4 mm darker chips; the page adds a planar reflection on it

lift.used_for: lift box: plate, band, cap, brushed steel

lift_lintel.used_for: lift wall above its opening, dark frame

stairs.used_for: stair box: plate, band, cap, concrete

corridor_borrowed.used_for: translucent: corridor floor the route graph borrows from another floor (not in this floor's map data)

floor_bridged.used_for: translucent: floor strip under an edge bridging a gap in the corridor data

door_uncertain.used_for: translucent amber panel filling the opening of a door whose position was guessed (z+0.02..z+2.2)

ceiling.used_for: ceiling at z+3.0 (underside of the ceiling plate)

roof.used_for: top and edges of the ceiling plate: the dark roof where no floor is above

facade_glass.used_for: exterior walls z+0.9..z+3: blue-green tinted curtain wall with thin faint mullion lines (translucent through the texture)

facade_sill.used_for: exterior walls z..z+0.9: aluminium sill panel

frame_dark.used_for: dark door frames (jambs and head), flush with the wall, only where a room's own door, a lift or stair entry or an entrance cuts a real wall; none at zones, titled corridors, neighbours' walls or doors off any wall

glass_pane.used_for: tinted glass: side panels beside office / meeting room doors, balustrades at the atrium void

column.used_for: round columns at the atrium void (generic), plain mid light grey

downlight.used_for: recessed ceiling downlights over corridors every 3 m (emissive discs, generic)

skylight.used_for: skylight over the atrium void on the top void level (emissive)

atrium_facade.used_for: the foyer atrium's walls: silver-grey aluminium panels with dark joints and deep-set square blue-glass windows, two bays by two storeys per texture tile (windows alternate storey to storey)

atrium_roof.used_for: the atrium's coffered skylight roof seen from below: a square grid of deep grey coffers, diamonds against the walls (which run at 45 degrees)

atrium_light.used_for: warm spotlights at the crossings of the coffer grid (emissive)

granite.used_for: level 2's foyer and lobbies: polished light grey speckled granite in 600 mm tiles; the page adds a planar reflection on it

granite_step.used_for: the steps and the raised landing up to the Alibaba lab: the foyer's granite, without the page's floor reflection (it mirrors only at the foyer's floor height)

granite_link.used_for: level 6's glass link: mid-grey polished granite (team photo), without the page's floor reflection

nosing.used_for: yellow anti-slip nosing on the steps up to the Alibaba lab's landing

desk_wood.used_for: the information desk's orange wood counter

stair_white.used_for: the white spiral stair tower in the atrium: central fin, treads and landings

portal.used_for: the brushed metal portal round the Chua Thian Poh Chamber entrance; the stainless frame of the X-Frontiers doors at the end of level 6's glass link

roof_membrane.used_for: flat roofs open to the sky: a floor's top where no floor stands above (area 2 over level 6, the ledges round level 6, area 1 over level 9), pale grey membrane

roof_glazing.used_for: glazed roofs seen from above: the foyer atrium's skylight, the round lobby's lantern, the rooflight over level 6's wing corridor

roof_plant.used_for: plant rooms, lift overruns and stair housings on the roof of area 2 (MazeMap's level 7 shapes there; heights generic)

spandrel.used_for: the facade band between a floor's ceiling and the next slab (z+3.0..z+4.2); on a roof it is the parapet, with a metal coping

diffuser.used_for: linear slot diffusers along both sides of the ceiling of level 6's glass link (team photo)

sign_ctp.used_for: a sign on the atrium's walls (team photos): CHUA THIAN POH / Chamber For Entrepreneurship Education

sign_info.used_for: a sign on the atrium's walls (team photos): INFORMATION

sign_academy.used_for: a sign on the atrium's walls (team photos): NTU Entrepreneurship Academy

sign_borderx.used_for: a sign on the atrium's walls (team photos): BORDER X Block

sign_frontiers.used_for: a sign on the atrium's walls (team photos): X-FRONTIERS Block

sign_angel.used_for: a sign on the atrium's walls (team photos): Alibaba-NTU Global / e-Sustainability CorpLab

palette.terrazzo: #a3a19e (texture-darkened, with a planar reflection in the page)

style.modelled_from_data: slabs, corridor plates, every wall, opening, lift and stair box, the atrium void (corridor hole of floors 3-5) and the exterior walls (floor outline)
style.generic_not_surveyed: mullion lines, terrazzo speckle, ceilings at 3.0 m and the roof, downlight positions, the four columns, door frames, glass side panels, balustrade design, skylight, the facade band and parapets, the heights of the roof's plant, overruns and housings, the glass link's posts, rails and diffusers

void.note: the atrium circle from the corridor data; two lift shafts stand inside it (the lift tower) and the floor bridges to them stay, so the open void is the circle minus cores and bridges

floor_offsets.what: the landing at the top of the steps

data_gaps: Floor 8 has only fragments of corridor in MazeMap: the corridors the route graph adds from floor 9 are drawn as a translucent plate (material corridor_borrowed); the slab there = floor outline + rooms + a 1 m strip under every graph edge

Floors 2 and 6 have no corridor polygons in MazeMap: their walkways come from the team's site notes (map/site-corrections.json); level 6's corridors, lifts and stairs are level 5's (cut back where level 6's rooms stand), its area 2 set back to the roof's outline, its rooms copied only where floors 3-5 agree (map/derive_level6.py)
Level 7 over area 2 in MazeMap is the roof of level 6 (team): drawn as roof, not as a floor
Edges whose hint starts '(corridor data incomplete' bridge a gap in the corridor data: the floor strip under them is translucent (material floor_bridged)

Door nodes labelled 'door position guessed': their opening is filled with a translucent amber panel (material door_uncertain) and listed in uncertain_doors with the corridor-facing wall segment, for a dashed outline

Openings of kind 'crossing' are where the route graph passes through a drawn wall (mostly the borrowed corridors of floor 8, level 6's corridors copied from level 5, and door stubs of rooms that do not touch a corridor): confirm on site

camera_paths.note: per walk edge, a polyline the camera follows at eye height keeping clearance_m from every wall face and stopping door_stop_m before a door; the page and route.json use it instead of the straight graph edge
